notes.title: New Feature - Private Matches
notes.content:
[p]Greetings fellow Scrappers![/p][p][/p][p]This week, we're pushing an important update to the Demo build: Private Matches! This has been something we've been working on for the last few weeks, and in light of feedback received during Next Fest, we decided to prioritize the feature, rather than wait for a larger multiplayer update we have planned for the fall.[/p][p][/p][p]The Private Match feature allows players to create 1v1 lobbies to challenge their friends directly, rather than using the regular Online PVP queue. Here's how it works:[/p][p][/p][p][/p][olist][*][p]On the main menu, players now have a 'Private Match' button. Selecting this will open the Private Match sub menu.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45434841/75be35c95ddba2893da9146cf2506054796e2216.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p][/p][/*][*][p]Once the host (Player 1) selects the Private Match menu, they are given the option to create a Private Lobby.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45434841/f2bd75cffd938fe13bcb4fd7bbc122c3fa3c0d9f.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p][/p][/*][*][p]The Private Lobby will automatically generate a five-digit, alphanumeric code that can be given out to a second player to join.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45434841/89cf9e695dec7f802a3fb460720afca9cb89ce47.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p][/p][/*][*][p]The Client (Player 2) can then enter the Private Match menu and enter the 5-digit code to join the lobby. Note: these codes are NOT case sensitive.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45434841/ab316ac2fa8609d635b150bf31e236727d4fd4f5.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p][/p][/*][*][p]Once the challenger joins the lobby, everything functions identical to a normal PVP match.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45434841/29aaace96ce6c120ae6d497296a212667bad3496.png"][/img][/p][/*][/olist][p]And that's it! it's now easier than ever to challenge your friends to a few rounds in your favorite arena![/p][p][/p][p]As always, our team wants to know how new features and updates feel to our community, so please submit feedback via the link in the Main Menu.

Until next time![/p][p][/p][p]-William (Project Director @ 301)[/p][p][/p]

notes.title: JUNK! 2025 Roadmap
notes.content: [p]Greetings Scrappers![/p][p][/p][p]The first half of 2025 has been exceedingly busy for us at 301. We launched our JUNK! Playtest in January, attended GDC 2025 in March, launched the JUNK! Demo in May, and took part in Next Fest in June, introducing the game to new players and our small but mighty community at every step of the way. I'm so very appreciative of everyone who's downloaded our game and played a few rounds, and even more thankful to those who have provided feedback so that JUNK! starts becoming the best version of itself.[/p][p][/p][p]With all of this said, we’re only just getting started. I want to share some details regarding our development roadmap for the second half of 2025, and what we're hoping to accomplish.[/p][p][/p][olist][*][p]We're currently working on an overhaul to our matchmaking system and are building out a way for players to create and join custom lobbies. This will let Scrappers challenge their friends directly so that they aren't waiting to see if a lobby opens or constantly battling against the AI opponents. The matchmaking overhaul will likely be rolled out in phases as some parts of this process are easier/faster to implement than others. We'll be sure to communicate what feature is launching when and with clear details on how each addition or change works.[/p][/*][*][p]We're building a proper single player ladder-style campaign. Similar to classic fighting games from the 90s, where the player battles against a pre-set order of increasingly difficult opponents in specific settings, our single player mode will act as a way for Scrappers to experience each arena and opponent all while the difficulty and rewards increase as they fight closer and closer to becoming a League champion.[/p][/*][*][p]We have a handful of new robot characters in development that Scrappers will be able to choose from. As they're completed and included in the game, we'll be reworking the Shop so that Scrappers will be able to choose an initial, free robot from our list of characters. Afterward, the rest of the characters will need to be unlocked in-game, the same as abilities are currently.[/p][/*][*][p]It's our goal to finalize our demo's feature set and then begin shifting over to our Early Access phase by the end of the year. I don't want to promise specific dates on when this will happen, but upon the Early Access launch, the JUNK! demo version will limit future updates to bug fixes and performance updates, and JUNK!'s Early Access version will be the where new robots, arenas, paint jobs, abilities, etc. will be released. To be clear, if we decide to overhaul things like the game's UI or reward systems, obviously those updates will be included in future versions of our Demo release. It's our intention to build the very best introduction to our game as possible, where players can come back again and again, challenge their friends, upgrade their robots, explore new and novel environments, and have a lot of fun.[/p][/*][/olist][p][/p][p]Thank you all for coming on this journey with us! We'll share more updates as we update our demo and prepare for Early Access, and we hope you enjoy playing JUNK! as much as we enjoy making it.[/p][p][/p][p]-William (Project Director @ 301)[/p][p][/p]

notes.title: Next Fest is Here!
notes.content: [p]Next Fest is here![/p][p][/p][p]It's been a grind, but the team at 301 are excited to be included in Steam's June 2025 Next Fest event.[/p][p]While JUNK! (A Demo About Robots) is still very much a work in progress, we wanted to share our game with everyone while we're working towards an Early Access release sometime later this year. Our primary goal in taking part in Next Fest is to gain as much feedback, both good and bad, about our game so that future releases are able to exceed expectations of our target player base. [/p][p]So far, we've received a handful of notes on what features we should include as well as a few bug reports that we'd missed in testing. We want to extend our thanks to everyone who's taking a few minutes to play the game, and share their experiences, and look forward to fulfilling those expectations over the coming weeks and months.[/p][p]Thank you everyone who has taken a moment to check out our game! We look forward to seeing you in the arena again soon![/p][p][/p][p]-William (Project Director @ 301)[/p][p][/p]

notes.content:
Corrected two outstanding bugs:

[*] Fixed issue where Client fails to connect to Host when launching match (outstanding PVP issue)
[*] Fixed issue where game was incorrectly scaling full screen setting (outstanding resolution issue)

notes.title: Update 20250529
notes.content:
I want to extend a huge thank you to everyone who has downloaded and played our demo this week! We're elated that so many people have either clicked that Download Demo button or have wish listed our game. We're digging into the feedback we've received and are evaluating changes to make JUNK! more fun for new players, and to correct a small list of bugs that have been encountered.

Improvements:
[olist]
[*] Reduced Level Requirements for most abilities (improving experience and reducing 'grind')
[*] Updated feedback form
[*] Added Discord Button to main menu UI
[*] Updated credits
[/olist]

Known Bugs:
[olist]
[*] PVP has issues where match is not accurately closed on back end, causing crashes when joining new matches (since the old match still 'exists'). We're reviewing networking code and extensively testing to solve this problem
[*] Significant display resolution issue when launching app on SteamDeck, currently researching a solution
[/olist]
